export_note: Selected fields from the completed native grade; machine-local paths are omitted. The mathematical grade is preserved.

grade.first_issue: In Case 2, the claim that the distance from \(x_0\) to the forward orbit \(\{y+nc(y):n\in\mathbb N\}\) is at most \(c(y)\) is false when \(y>x_0\).
grade.summary: The solution correctly derives defect invariance, nonnegativity, and equality of all positive defect values. However, its decisive argument excluding coexistence of zero and positive defects relies on a false assertion, so constancy of \(c\) is not established as submitted.
strengths: Correctly obtains \(f^{(n)}(x)=x+nc(x)\), \(c(x)\ge0\), and proves that any two positive defect values coincide.
Correctly verifies that every \(f(x)=x+c\), \(c\ge0\), satisfies the inequalities.

errors.description: The false forward-orbit distance claim invalidates the entire mixed zero/positive defect case and all subsequent interval propagation.
